title: Helicity-Selective Electron-Phonon Coupling Between $PT$-Partner States in $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$
abstract: Rotational symmetry ($C_n$) constrains chiral phonons, but how other symmetries affect their interactions remains largely unexplored. We perform a theoretical and computational study of chiral phonon coupling to parity-time ($PT$)-degenerate electron doublets in $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$. Although $PT$ suppresses phonon singlet chirality, chiral phonon doublets can helically interact with $PT$-partner electronic states via a mechanism similar to pseudospin. Selection rules are then analyzed with the interplay of $PT$ and $C_3$. Our computational results of $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$ suggest chiral phonons may be used to resolve intravalley electronic states in $PT$ systems.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes how $C_3$ and $	ext{PT}$ symmetries govern the electron-phonon coupling in $2H$-bilayer $	ext{MoS}_2$. The authors demonstrate that these symmetries enforce strict chiral selection rules on the coupling strength. This mechanism suggests that chiral phonons can be used as a tool to spectroscopically resolve distinct electronic states within the same momentum valley of $	ext{PT}$ materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how symmetries, specifically Parity-Time (PT) and $C_3$ rotational symmetry, constrain the chiral coupling between phonons and $	ext{PT}$-degenerate electron doublets.
main_result: Chiral phonons can establish helicity-selective coupling rules, allowing for the resolution of intravalley electronic states within $	ext{PT}$ systems.
method: The authors employed theoretical and computational methods, including DFT/DFPT calculations, to analyze the electron-phonon coupling Hamiltonian under symmetry constraints.
model_or_system: The physical system is $2H$-bilayer $	ext{MoS}_2$. The model focuses on the electron-phonon coupling ($	ext{EPC}$) Hamiltonian ($	ext{H}'_{\Gamma K}$) involving $	ext{PT}$-partnered electronic states described by a pseudospin.
key_observables: Chiral phonon coupling strengths ($\sqrt{\lambda}$), $C_3$ eigenvalues ($\chi$), and the overlap matrix $S_{mn}$ are key diagnostics.
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to the interplay between $	ext{PT}$ symmetry and $C_3$ symmetry, particularly the helicity of the phonons ($	ext{Q}_{\pm}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of symmetry rules derived for $C_3$ to other $PT$ $C_n$ systems and utilizes DFT/DFPT results for coupling strengths.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phonon dispersion, the atomic structure, and schematics detailing the chiral $	ext{PT}$-based $	ext{EPC}$ interaction, showing how coupling strengths vary based on phonon helicity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the symmetry constraints imposed by $	ext{PT}$ and $C_3$ on the $	ext{EPC}$ Hamiltonian. It then analyzes three distinct cases based on the $C_3$ eigenvalues of the electronic doublets to derive specific chiral selection rules. Finally, it applies these rules to predict the selective coupling mechanism.
why_interesting: The explicit use of symmetry constraints ($C_3$ and $	ext{PT}$) to predict highly selective coupling mechanisms (helicity-selectivity) is relevant to understanding open quantum systems where environmental coupling dictates observable dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Phonon dispersion for 2H-bilayer MoS2, with the 2D symmetry irreps labeled in red. We see that 2H hosts several doubly degenerate irreps at Γ, for which chiral combinations may be formed and the helicity-selective coupling to the PT-induced electron pseudospin may be observed.
FIG. 2: Atomic structure of 2H-bilayer MoS2. Notably, the lattice contains an inversion center, an example of which we have denoted with a red point.

FIG. 3: (Left) Band structure of 2H-bilayer MoS2, wherein we have highlighted and given a schematic for the chiral PT-based electron-phonon interaction (right). The valence band maximum has been shifted to zero. The selected electron states that couple to the Qν,+ and Qν,−phonons are labeled by a, b respectively and are related by PT within an initial/final doublet. Moreover, chiral selectivity shows that Qν,−, Qν,+ have zero coupling with a, b states, respectively. In 2H bilayer MoS2, the initial conduction band states are dependent on phonon mode, since the initial electron subspace has real C3 eigenvalues and therefore are not constrained by rotational symmetry.
